newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma plans budget hearings on May 20.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma plans budget hearings on May 20.

text.p: Russia's State Duma lower house of parliament will start hearings on government plans to cut spending on May 20 and debate the bill on May 21, the head of the Duma's budget committee said on Tuesday.

Committee chairman Mikhail Zadornov, speaking to reporters, confirmed that the sequester bill would be debated on May 21 after Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin presents a report on spending and revenues in the first quarter.

Revenues have been well below budgeted levels so far this year. Under the 1997 budget, the government must propose spending cuts, or a sequester, to the Duma, if revenues fall below 90 percent of planned levels in any quarter.
But the Duma is unlikely to give the government an easy ride.
Zadornov said the Duma's agenda-setting council would decide on May 14 whether to ask the Audit Chamber, which monitors government spending on behalf of parliament, to examine the sequester bill.
And senior communist deputy Viktor Ilyukhin said the Duma would consider alternatives to the government's own sequester bill on May 21.
"Our starting point is that the government can borrow to normalise the rhythm of our economy," Ilyukhin, who is chairman of the Duma's security committee, told reporters.

Ilyukhin said money supply currently accounted for only 12-16 percent of gross domestic product, which was not enough for the economy to work properly, and money supply needed to be increased to provide additional resources.
The government has ruled out printing money to ease the current payments crisis.
